question: Using elementary row transformations on the matrix and the identity matrix simultaneously, find the inverse of $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{bmatrix}$$ and verify the result by matrix multiplication.
explanation:
Applying Matrix Transformations

To obtain the inverse by row transformations, apply the same elementary row operations simultaneously to $A$ and $I$. Begin with $$\left[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1&2&1&0\\2&5&0&1\end{array}\right]$$ Apply $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$. Then $$\left[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1&2&1&0\\0&1&-2&1\end{array}\right]$$ Now apply $R_1\to R_1-2R_2$. We obtain $$\left[\begin{array}{cc|cc}1&0&5&-2\\0&1&-2&1\end{array}\right]$$ Thus, the matrix on the left has been transformed into the identity matrix, and hence $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

Now, $$AA^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=I$$ Also, $$A^{-1}A=\begin{bmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=I$$ Therefore, the inverse exists, $A$ is invertible, and $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix}$$.
